items.title: Federal jury convicts man of arson in deadly Palisades Fire
items.feedTitle: Federal jury convicts man of starting the deadly 2025 Palisades Fire in Los Angeles
items.summary: A federal jury found Jonathan Rinderknecht, 30, guilty of arson for starting the January 2025 Palisades Fire in Los Angeles, which killed 12 people and destroyed over 6,800 buildings. Prosecutors argued he had been "mad at everything" in the days before the fire. The conviction comes after a mistrial earlier in the year, and represents a major step in holding someone accountable for one of California's deadliest recent wildfires.

items.title: Missouri judge approves $7.25 billion Bayer Roundup settlement
items.feedTitle: Court approves $7.25 billion Bayer settlement over claims Roundup weed killer caused cancer
items.summary: A Missouri judge approved Bayer's $7.25 billion settlement to resolve thousands of claims from U.S. cancer patients who alleged the company's weed killer Roundup caused lymphoma. The settlement, payable over two decades, resolves litigation that has weighed heavily on the German agrochemical maker. The court's approval marks a major resolution of one of the largest product liability cases in recent years.

items.title: Federal appeals court voids pandemic-era proxy voting law
items.feedTitle: Pandemic-era law passed unconstitutionally because of proxy voting, appeals court rules
items.summary: A federal appeals court ruled that a pandemic-era spending bill passed in 2022 was unconstitutional because the House used proxy voting to pass it. The ruling has broader implications for other legislation passed during the pandemic using the same remote voting method. The decision raises questions about the validity of laws passed during COVID-19 emergency procedures.

items.title: Trump administration replaces cybersecurity chief amid tech outages
items.feedTitle: Mounting tech disruptions raise concerns about U.S. cybersecurity
items.summary: President Trump replaced the nation's top cybersecurity official following a string of technology outages over recent weeks. While officials stressed the outages were not from intentional attacks, the incidents have raised concerns about U.S. cybersecurity infrastructure as AI capabilities grow. The leadership change signals the administration's focus on addressing systemic vulnerabilities.

items.title: Princeton neuroscientist detained by ICE at D.C. airport
items.feedTitle: Princeton student detained by ICE at D.C. airport is being held in Virginia
items.summary: A Chinese-born Princeton neuroscientist was detained by ICE at Ronald Reagan Washington National Airport and is being held in Virginia. The detention highlights ongoing concerns about immigration enforcement and the treatment of international scholars. Details about the specific circumstances and charges remain limited, though the case has drawn attention from academic circles.

stlouis.title: MetroLink extension to airport opens November 30
stlouis.feedTitle: MetroLink extension to MidAmerica St. Louis Airport gets opening date
stlouis.summary: The MetroLink extension to MidAmerica St. Louis Airport is set to begin service on November 30, expanding regional transit access to the airport. The project represents a major infrastructure development for the St. Louis metro area, providing direct rail connection to the airport for the first time. Service launch follows months of preparation and testing.

stlouis.title: St. Louis-based Rawlings gets new majority owner
stlouis.feedTitle: St. Louis-based Rawlings gets new majority owner
stlouis.summary: Rawlings, the St. Louis-based sporting goods company, has announced a new majority owner. The ownership change signals a potential shift in the company's strategic direction. Details on the new ownership structure and future operations remain to be seen.

stlouis.title: Two beloved St. Louis area restaurants closing in 2027
stlouis.feedTitle: 2 Beloved St. Louis Area Restaurants Closing Their Doors in 2027
stlouis.summary: Two beloved restaurants in the St. Louis area have announced they will be closing their doors in 2027. The closures represent a loss to the local dining scene and community. The specific reasons for closure were not detailed in available reports.

items.title: Russian missile strike kills two in Zelenskyy's hometown
items.feedTitle: Russian strike kills two, wounds 60, in Zelenskyy’s hometown
items.summary: Russian forces struck the city of Kryvyi Rih in central Ukraine—President Zelenskyy's hometown—with ballistic missiles, killing at least 2 people and wounding approximately 60 others. The attack comes as Russian missiles also landed in NATO member Poland, escalating tensions in the region. U.S.-led peace efforts continue to face uncertainty amid the ongoing strikes.

items.title: Magnitude 6.8 earthquake rocks Timor-Leste, shakes Australia
items.feedTitle: Shaking reported in Australia after magnitude 6.8 earthquake rocks Timor-Leste, Pacific Ring of Fire
items.summary: A magnitude 6.8 earthquake struck Timor-Leste in the Pacific Ring of Fire, with shaking also reported across Australia. The quake occurred in a seismically active region. No immediate casualty reports or significant damage assessments were available at time of reporting.

items.title: UK and EU strike landmark post-Brexit trade and ties deal
items.feedTitle: European Union and UK strike a 'landmark deal' to strengthen ties after Brexit
items.summary: The United Kingdom and European Union have reached a landmark deal to strengthen ties after Brexit, covering trade, emissions, food standards, and youth exchange programs. Foreign Secretary Ed Miliband said "all options are open" in future discussions, including potential rejoining of the EU. The agreement represents the most significant reset in UK-EU relations since the 2020 Brexit vote.

items.title: Denmark expels Russian diplomat over alleged murder plot
items.feedTitle: Denmark to expel Russian diplomat over alleged plot to kill US-Ukrainian rapper
items.summary: Denmark's government said it would expel Russia's defence attaché in Copenhagen after Moscow was suspected of planning to assassinate US-Ukrainian rapper Kyivstoner before a concert. The alleged plot is attributed to Russian intelligence. Russia's embassy has denied the allegations, but the expulsion marks an escalation in Nordic-Russian tensions.

items.title: UN's highest court finds Myanmar guilty of genocide against Rohingya
items.feedTitle: Rights groups urge sanctions after ICJ finds Myanmar guilty of genocide against Rohingya
items.summary: The International Court of Justice ruled Thursday that Myanmar's military-backed government is guilty of genocide against Rohingya Muslims, ordering the country to allow returnees safe passage, pay reparations, and prosecute those suspected of genocide. However, the ICJ has no enforcement power. Rights groups are now urging international sanctions and accountability measures.

items.title: Toxic liquor kills 11, poisons 180 in Manipur state
items.feedTitle: Illicit alcohol kills 11, poisons 180 in northeast India’s Manipur state
items.summary: Illicit alcohol claimed at least 11 lives and hospitalized approximately 180 people in India's northeastern Manipur state. The deadly hooch tragedy highlights ongoing public health and law enforcement challenges in the region. Opposition leader Rahul Gandhi blamed the state government's negligence for the tragedy, while authorities have made arrests.

items.title: India to host WorldSkills Asia 2027 in Greater Noida
items.feedTitle: India to host WorldSkills Asia 2027 in Greater Noida, announces PM Modi
items.summary: Prime Minister Narendra Modi announced that India will host WorldSkills Asia 2027 in Greater Noida, showcasing the nation's vocational training capabilities. The event reflects India's focus on skill development as part of its broader development agenda. It aligns with Modi's repeated emphasis on technical skills and workforce preparation.

items.title: 14-year-old hacker arrested for Agniveer portal breach
items.feedTitle: 14-year-old hacker held for trying to sell private data of 4,000 Agniveers on dark web: Delhi Police
items.summary: Delhi Police apprehended a 14-year-old from Haryana for hacking the Agniveer recruitment test portal and attempting to sell private data of approximately 4,000 Agniveers on the dark web for $500. The teenager used an AI chatbot to identify valuable data and find portal access. Preliminary investigation suggests only names and addresses were accessed before the breach was discovered.

items.title: Cricketer Yuzvendra Chahal joins BJP, gets OBC Morcha role
items.feedTitle: Cricketer Yuzvendra Chahal joins BJP, gets role in OBC morcha executive committee
items.summary: Professional cricketer Yuzvendra Chahal joined the BJP and was appointed as a special invitee to the party's OBC (Other Backward Classes) Morcha executive committee. The appointment reflects the party's efforts to broaden its appeal across demographic groups. Chahal becomes another high-profile sports figure to join the ruling party.

items.title: Meta faces protests in India, gets 7-day ultimatum from opposition
items.feedTitle: Meta faces protests in India after accounts removed, gets 7-day ultimatum from opposition party
items.summary: India's opposition party, the Indian Youth Congress, issued a seven-day ultimatum to Meta after the platform removed accounts without clear explanation. The party is staging protests demanding the company lift restrictions and restore removed accounts. Meta faces growing scrutiny in India over content moderation and account removal policies.

immigration.title: H-1B delays and Trump rules drive skilled workers to exit US
immigration.feedTitle: Is America losing Indian talent? H-1B delays and Trump’s rules drive workers to the exit
immigration.summary: Rising delays in H-1B visa processing and tighter Trump administration rules are prompting skilled tech workers to abandon U.S. jobs and seek opportunities abroad, particularly in the UK and other nations. Bloomberg reports that companies including IBM have reduced sponsorship of H-1B positions. The trend reflects growing uncertainty among foreign workers about their ability to build careers and secure permanent status in the U.S.

immigration.title: Labor Department proposes sweeping PERM green card overhaul
immigration.feedTitle: Modernizing the Labor Market Test and Improving Protections for U.S. Workers in the PERM Immigrant Visa Program
immigration.summary: The U.S. Department of Labor has proposed major changes to the PERM (Permanent Employment-Based Immigration) labor certification process—proposed, not final. The rule would strengthen standards for employers sponsoring foreign workers, end Schedule A occupations, lengthen the layoff bar, and require more robust labor market testing. The proposal is the first major overhaul of the program in nearly 20 years. Healthcare workers and hospitals have flagged concerns about impacts on nursing recruitment.

immigration.title: H-4 EAD rescission remains on DHS long-term agenda
immigration.feedTitle: H-4 EAD Rescission Still Parked on DHS Long-Term Agenda - immigration-analytics.com
immigration.summary: The H-4 EAD (work permit for spouses of H-1B visa holders) rescission proposal remains parked on the Department of Homeland Security's long-term agenda—proposed, not finalized. The rule would strip work authorization from hundreds of thousands of spouses, predominantly affecting Indian nationals. No timeline for finalization has been announced, leaving visa holders in uncertainty about future policy.

items.title: Goldman Sachs warns AI 'unwind' poses deeper market danger
items.feedTitle: Goldman Sachs admits the 'AI unwind' has spiraled into something more dangerous — and it's watching for 3 signs of bottom
items.summary: Goldman Sachs said the AI sector selloff has evolved into something more dangerous than a simple tech correction, suggesting the downturn could worsen. The bank is monitoring three warning signs for market bottom. Volatility index (VIX) has surged near historical maximums, signaling extreme market fear and panic selling.

items.title: Indian markets surge despite global rout, Nifty near record high
items.feedTitle: Nifty, Sensex extend gains for 4th week amid strong foreign inflows
items.summary: While global markets tumbled, Indian stocks rallied for a fourth consecutive week, with the Nifty 50 hitting a nine-month high near 25,800 on record foreign investor inflows exceeding 1 trillion rupees in November. The Sensex surged nearly 900 points. Indian equity markets have outperformed global peers, with Bank Nifty up nearly 17.5% in a month as PSU and private banks gain. This divergence reflects strong FPI confidence in India amid global volatility.

items.title: Bitcoin falls to two-year low as global markets sink
items.feedTitle: Bitcoin Falls to More Than Two-Year Low as Global Markets Sink
items.summary: Bitcoin has fallen to its lowest level in more than two years as the broader stock market downturn has dragged crypto lower. The asset, often billed as "digital gold," failed to hold its safe-haven status during the selloff. Bitcoin's decline reflects the correlation between risk assets in a panic environment.

items.title: Trump ends penny minting after nearly 250 years
items.feedTitle: Trump formally ends minting of the penny after nearly 250 years of production
items.summary: President Trump signed the "Common Cents Act," formally ending U.S. penny production after nearly 250 years. The move reflects long-standing arguments that the coin's production cost exceeds its face value. Cash payments will need new rounding protocols absent the penny, though digital payments continue unaffected.

finance.note: Oil prices fell mid-week on demand concerns from the global market selloff, while U.S. stocks suffered their worst week of 2026—S&P 500 and Dow in correction territory, Nasdaq erasing all 2026 gains. Indian markets bucked the trend, with Nifty hitting 9-month highs on record FPI inflows, suggesting capital rotation toward emerging markets. Watch Monday for Fed communications on rate outlook and whether equity stabilization holds.

cards.title: Clarity beats complexity in crisis
cards.insight: During market turmoil (this week's AI selloff), companies and leaders who clearly explain *why* a crisis happened and *what* comes next retain credibility better than those offering vague reassurance. Goldman Sachs' naming of three warning signs gave traders a framework; vague 'hold steady' messaging gets ignored.
cards.takeaway: When explaining bad news, lead with one clear cause and one clear next step—not five caveats and ten possibilities.

cards.title: Numbers persuade when narrative fails
cards.insight: India's markets rose despite global chaos because one number—1+ trillion rupees in FPI inflows—outshouts all talk of recession. Conversely, Anthropic's IPO hype evaporated when the broader market number (Nasdaq down 9%) contradicted the company narrative.
cards.takeaway: In persuasion, a single robust metric beats eloquent argument. Find and repeat the number that proves your point.

cards.title: Urgency without deadlines kills trust
cards.insight: India's Youth Congress gave Meta a 7-day 'ultimatum' but it's unclear what enforcement mechanism exists. Trump threatened 'tremendous penalties' on tech firms building data centers abroad but offered no details or timeline. Threats without teeth invite dismissal and breed skepticism.
cards.takeaway: If you name a deadline or threat, have a visible enforcement mechanism ready or don't mention it.

cards.title: Proof-by-absence persuades academics but not markets
cards.insight: Anthropic's claim that Claude proved the Riemann hypothesis was mathematically exciting but stock price fell anyway because investors care about *commercializable impact*, not proof elegance. Stanford's competing all-human draft hours later muddied the narrative further.
cards.takeaway: Before claiming breakthrough, ask: does this sell to customers or only to peers? If only peers, it's research, not marketing.

ai.title: Anthropic mathematician claims Riemann hypothesis proof using Claude
ai.feedTitle: Anthropic mathematician claims he used Claude to prove 19th-century Riemann hypothesis
ai.summary: Levent Alpöge, a mathematician at Anthropic, claims to have used the company's Claude AI tool to prove the Riemann hypothesis—one of mathematics' most famous unsolved problems involving prime numbers. The claimed proof took six weeks using Claude and represents a potential historic breakthrough, though verification by the broader math community could take weeks or longer. Stanford released a competing all-human draft of a proof hours after Anthropic's claim.

ai.title: Anthropic IPO collides with tech's worst week since 2020
ai.feedTitle: Anthropic’s record IPO collides with tech’s worst week on Wall Street since 2020
ai.summary: Anthropic's record $93.5 billion IPO debut crashed into Wall Street's worst week for tech stocks since the COVID-19 pandemic. The AI startup's public market premiere failed to buoy sentiment as investors questioned the massive capital outlays being poured into AI infrastructure buildout. The company raised significant cash but stock performance disappointed amid broader tech sector selloff.

ai.title: U.S. Commerce closes cloud loophole enabling China AI chip access
ai.feedTitle: US Commerce Department closes cloud loophole that let Chinese firms rent AI chips
ai.summary: The U.S. Department of Commerce has closed a regulatory loophole that allowed Chinese firms to rent advanced U.S. AI chips through cloud services, circumventing export controls. The move tightens restrictions on how foreign entities access cutting-edge semiconductor technology. The closure addresses a key vulnerability in Trump's efforts to limit China's access to frontier AI capabilities.

ai.title: Chinese AI models trained using U.S. chips in domestic data centers
ai.feedTitle: Data centers full of U.S. chips are serving Chinese AI models–undermining Trump’s tech ambitions
ai.summary: Data centers full of U.S.-made AI chips are actively serving Chinese AI models, undermining the Trump administration's strategy to restrict China's access to advanced semiconductor technology. The workaround—keeping chips domestically in cloud facilities rather than exporting them directly—reveals gaps in export control enforcement. The issue complicates efforts to maintain U.S. technological advantage in AI.
